page_note: This page is entirely Mani-autobiographical / apostolic narrative material. The first-person speaker recounts persecution by the kings of the Assyrians, taking counsel with archons and eparchs, generals, Caesars, governors — and his journey to the land of the Medes and Parthians where he found 'the likeness of Wisdom.' None of this is impersonal cosmological substrate; both sides of every reference (Assyrians, Medes, Parthians, Caesars, eparchs) reach into the editor's contemporary geopolitical world. Segment 26 has an explicit dialogue-frame seam ('Then said the Apostle to that disciple'), after which Mani speaks in first person ('Since I am one Anointed, I came to the world...'). Heavy lacunae throughout (97% damage). Editorial fatigue score confirms massive drift toward apostolic_dialogue in second half. No core teaching extractable.
